scope: Two minimum-length corollaries, two padding displays and their proof; not full release acceptance

main.tex:cor:six-C5-minimum-length.reason: All three clauses now have actual matrix-level theorems. minimum_length quantifies over arbitrary n, ExactCode n 2 d with d >= 3, arbitrary local U(2) matrices and their literal tensor-kernel action on the orthonormal encoding. Projective order five is orderOf of the faithful adjoint representation of the logical unitary; its kernel consists exactly of scalar matrices. KL-preserving ancilla padding and the exact A1 recurrence give positive A1 when n < 6. The local eigenbasis construction preserves the full distance and LU class and changes the logical matrix only by a unit scalar; the quotient/matrix bridge supplies an actual intrinsic element of order five. Six-qubit rigidity therefore forces A1 = 0. canonical_attains uses the explicit c36,d36 states, with the same logical matrix/projective-order interface; six_qubit_lu_unique_of_distance_ge_three supplies uniqueness under the actual LU relation including physical permutations. This does not certify the following full-transversal-group/Clifford prose consequence or the unqualified Singleton display.

supplementary.tex:eq:main-order-five-pad.reason: projector_padFrame gives the literal computational-basis matrix entries of P tensored with m zero-state projectors, for arbitrary m including zero. padCode constructs the padded exact code from the original code; hasDistance_padFrame proves all KL equations at the same requested distance. Identity extension of the physical factors preserves the very same logical matrix, hence its projective order. minimum_length specializes m to 6-n under n<6.

For any positive rank K and any m, the normalized coefficient satisfies AWeight(padFrame F m,1) = AWeight(F,1)+m. The proof enumerates all four last-site Pauli labels using an actual finite equivalence and derives the full raw enumerator recurrence; the zero-weight term is K^2. Nonnegativity and m>0 give strict positivity. The lower-bound proof uses K=2 and m=6-n; there is no numerical approximation or supplied trace identity.
